newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Finance chief to testify on immigration boss.
newsitem.headline: HK Finance chief to testify on immigration boss.

text.p: Hong Kong's Finance Secretary Donald Tsang has been summoned to testify under oath to a legislative panel on the mysterious sudden retirement of the territory's immigration chief, an official said on Tuesday.

Tsang would appear before the Legislative Council inquiry panel this Thursday to answer questions about former Director of Immigration Laurence Leung, who took sudden early retirement in July, an official at the legislature's secretariat said.
In the absence of Governor Chris Patten and Chief Secretary Anson Chan, Tsang was acting governor of Hong Kong around the time that Leung stepped down on July 6.
Leung's successor, Regina Yipm will also testify on Thursday along with Leung's secretary and the secretary of Hong Kong's civil service chief.

Leung, who had worked for 30 years in the Hong Kong government, was responsible for passports and immigration security, highly sensitive areas in the run-up to Hong Kong's transfer from Britain to China next July 1.
At the time, he said he was resigning for personal reasons, and Patten has declined to say if there were other reasons.
Politicians in Hong Kong say they are anxious to know whether there is any truth in newspaper allegations concerning his abrupt departure.
Leung wrote to a Hong Kong newspaper recently dismissing all the press allegations against him as untrue.
